title: Finite and disordered Kitaev chains: a large deviation study
authors: Clément Fortin, Kai Wang, Tami Pereg-Barnea
abstract: Topological edge states are celebrated for their robustness against disorder, yet the interplay between disorder and system size remains poorly understood. We use large deviations theory as a framework to study finite-size effects beyond the central limit theorem. We analyze Lyapunov exponent fluctuations in the static and periodically driven disordered Kitaev chain and find an asymmetry in the large deviations statistics that makes stronger edge localizations of Majorana zero modes exponentially more likely than weaker ones. We demonstrate that this fluctuation asymmetry is not tied to the topological phase. This asymmetry endows topological edge states with an additional protection against disorder and persists across a broad class of disorder distribution. We show how to use our framework to find the minimum system size required to satisfy topological quantum computing constraints.
summary: This work applies Large Deviations Theory to analyze the fluctuations of Lyapunov exponents governing Majorana edge modes in disordered Kitaev chains. The key finding is that these fluctuations exhibit a measurable asymmetry, which grants an additional protection mechanism to topological states against disorder. This provides new theoretical tools for assessing the stability and required size of quantum devices based on topological properties.
main_problem: The study investigates finite-size effects of topologically protected edge states, specifically analyzing fluctuations beyond the Central Limit Theorem in disordered quantum chains.
main_result: The fluctuation statistics of the Lyapunov exponent are found to be fundamentally asymmetric, providing an additional protection mechanism for topological edge states against disorder strength.
method: The analysis heavily relies on Large Deviations Theory (LDT) to derive rate functions ($I(x)$) that characterize the probability decay of deviations from the mean Lyapunov exponent.
model_or_system: The primary model is the disordered Kitaev chain, analyzed in both static and periodically driven regimes. The system supports Majorana zero modes (MZMs) at its edges.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponent ($L_N$), Rate Function ($I(x)$), Asymmetry measure ($\Delta P_N(\delta)$), Minimum required system size ($N$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), System size ($N$), Coupling constants ($t, \Delta$), Driving frequency ($\Omega$ or $T$).
main_assumptions: The disorder potentials ($\mu_n$) are assumed to be independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.), and the analysis often relies on power-law behavior of the probability density function near specific points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the rate function $I(x)$ showing characteristic asymmetries, phase diagrams mapping MZM/MPM hosting regions based on Lyapunov signs, and plots detailing how asymmetry is suppressed or restored by changing parameters like disorder strength ($W$) relative to critical values.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general framework using LDT for Lyapunov exponents in disordered systems. It then applies this theory sequentially to the static Kitaev chain, followed by the driven (Floquet) Kitaev chain, analyzing how asymmetry arises and changes based on disorder strength relative to driving parameters.
why_interesting: The discovery of an inherent fluctuation asymmetry that enhances topological protection is a powerful theoretical result for understanding robustness in quantum materials, providing quantitative metrics beyond simple phase diagrams.
